header.running_head: Remorse and Concern Because of Fleeing

blocks.text: Zaid (RA) informed him about what had transpired. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says that she had never heard a more detailed and accurate account of any incident given by someone who had been present there. When the defeated Muslim army returned and Hadhrat Umar (RA) noticed the anxiety of the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar because they had fled the battlefield, he said, "Do not worry, O assembly of Muslims! I am your base to which you have withdrawn (to replenish your strength before returning to battle)."
The Anxiety of Hadhrat Mu'aadh Qaari (RA) when he Fled During the Battle for the Bridge and the Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Husayn
blocks.text: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Husayn and others report that Hadhrat Mu'aadh Qaari (RA) from the Banu Najjaar tribe was amongst those who were present and had fled during the battle for the Bridge of Abu Ubayd. He always wept whenever he recited the following verse of the Qur'aan:

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَنْ يُّوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهٗٓ اِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِّقِتَالٍ اَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا اِلٰى فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ بَآءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللّٰهِ وَمَاْوٰىهُ جَهَنَّمُ ۗ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيْرُ
blocks.text: On such a day (of battle), whoever will turn his back to them with a reason other than altering the course of battle (such as pretending to flee so that the enemy follows them into an ambush) or (flees with a reason other than) retreating to (join with) another group (of Muslim soldiers so that their combined force can fight the enemy), then indeed he shall return with Allaah's anger and his abode shall be Jahannam (because deserting the battlefield is a major sin). What an evil place to return to!

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Husayn
blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) would then say to him, "Do not weep, O Mu'aadh. I am your base to whom you have retreated (to regroup and have reinforcements before launching another attack)."[^1]
Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubayd Qaari (RA) Returns to the Land of the Battle from which he fled to Redeem himself

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) says that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubayd (RA) was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ who was with the army that was defeated on the day that Hadhrat Abu Ubayd (RA) was martyred (at the bridge). He received the title of Qaari, a title that no other companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ received. Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said to him, "Do you wish to go to Shaam where the Muslims are in a weak position and the enemy are becoming bold against them.
